comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C3, C40-C45 regarding P118 identification through traditional screening assays. Both evaluations find the evidence supported, with reviewers praising the varied methods and impressive data generation that OpenEval also acknowledges.

Complete agreement on claims C62-C64, C118 regarding genomic characterization. Both find the whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatic analyses supported. OpenEval notes the need for experimental validation while reviewers praise the genomics approach as part of varied methods.

Full concordance on claims C19, C97-C98 regarding ecological modeling (null model and neutral community model). Both evaluations support these findings, with reviewers implicitly accepting the ecological framework as part of the comprehensive analysis.

Perfect agreement on claims C127-C131 regarding IAA's mechanism through AHR signaling in macrophages. Both find the in vitro mechanistic data supported, with reviewers noting the use of immunology methods and OpenEval highlighting the strong evidence from AHR inhibitor experiments.

Strong alignment on claims C132-C139 regarding macrophage depletion experiments. OpenEval addresses C132-C139 while peer review also includes C140. Both find compelling evidence for the essential role of macrophages, with reviewers praising the in vivo and in vitro confirmation studies.

High concordance on claims C120-C126 regarding IAA recapitulating protective effects. Both evaluations strongly support these findings. Peer review also includes C20 (main conclusion). Editor's summary explicitly affirms that a single metabolite can recapitulate probiotic effects.

Strong agreement on microbiota analysis claims C11-C13, C78-C93. OpenEval focuses on 16S rRNA sequencing data while peer review also includes C9, C94-C96. Both find the microbiota findings solid, though OpenEval notes some functional significance questions (e.g., Akkermansia reduction).

Good alignment on claims C50-C57 regarding antibacterial factor characterization. OpenEval addresses C4, C49-C58 while peer review focuses on C50-C57. Both support the protein/peptide-based antimicrobial conclusion with no concerns raised.

Strong concordance on untargeted metabolomics claims C99-C109. Peer review also includes C10, C14-C18, C110-C115 (broader metabolomics scope). Both evaluations support the metabolomics findings, with editor's summary explicitly affirming metabolite identification.

Moderate alignment on C. elegans screening claims C5, C47-C48, C59, C61. OpenEval also includes C46 while peer review includes C4, C49, C58, C60. Both support the C. elegans model validation, with reviewers commending varied methods and OpenEval noting statistical significance.

Partial overlap on murine protection claims. OpenEval addresses C65-C71 (survival, body weight, organ indices, bacterial burden) while peer review covers C6-C8, C65-C77 (including histological data). Both provide strong support, with reviewers noting compelling evidence and solid conclusions.

Moderate concordance on targeted metabolomics and correlation analysis. OpenEval addresses C14-C18, C110-C115 while peer review focuses on C110-C119. Both support the correlation findings, though OpenEval explicitly notes correlation does not establish causation.

Partial overlap on intestinal integrity claims C72-C77. OpenEval focuses specifically on histological and molecular protection data while peer review groups these with broader murine protection claims C6-C8, C65-C71. Both find multi-modal assessment compelling.

Partial alignment on microbiome-metabolome integration. OpenEval addresses C116-C117, C119 (network analysis and P118 metabolite production) while peer review covers broader correlation claims C110-C119. Both support the integrated analysis approach.

Limited overlap on tryptophan metabolite correlations C14-C18. OpenEval groups these with targeted metabolomics C110-C115 while peer review includes them with broader untargeted metabolomics C10, C99-C109. Both support the metabolite-protection correlations.

Minor overlap on antibacterial characterization claims C4, C49, C58. OpenEval addresses comprehensive antibacterial properties C4, C49-C58 while peer review groups C4, C49, C58 with C. elegans findings. Both support the antibacterial characterization.

Minimal overlap on main conclusion C20. OpenEval addresses C20, C140 as integrative conclusion while peer review includes C20 with IAA sufficiency claims C120-C126. Both strongly support the overall mechanistic conclusion.

Minimal overlap on claim C60 regarding heat-resistant protective factors. OpenEval separately evaluates C60-C61 while peer review groups C60 with broader C. elegans and antibacterial claims. Both support the finding of dual protective mechanisms.

Minimal overlap on integrative conclusion C140. OpenEval addresses C20, C140 as main conclusion while peer review includes C140 with macrophage depletion claims C132-C139. Both strongly affirm the mechanistic pathway conclusion.

OpenEval separately evaluated background/literature claims C1-C2, C21-C39 as supported context. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these background claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.
